issues.legal_issue: A second appeal under the Maharashtra Hereditary Offices Act, 1874, was not maintainable, and an improperly entertained second appeal could not be treated as a revision; the subsequent statutory revision was nevertheless maintainable.

The exemption under Section 88(1)(a) of the Maharashtra Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, applied only to Watan lands assigned as remuneration to an officiator under Section 23 of the 1874 Act, not to other Watan lands.
Sections 29 and 31 of the Tenancy Act applied to the Watan lands at issue, so the Watandar’s heirs could not recover possession from the tenants under Sections 5, 11, and 11A of the 1874 Act.
A lease challenged by pending proceedings remained subsisting on the appointed day despite the tenants’ interim loss of physical possession.

Under Section 8 of the Maharashtra Revenue Patels (Abolition of Offices) Act, 1962, tenants of Watan land whose lawful leases subsisted on the appointed day were entitled to the Tenancy Act’s benefits, including statutory purchase, once the exemption under Section 88CA ceased to apply.

The proviso to Section 8 of the Abolition Act deemed the lease to commence on the date of regrant only for calculating the purchase price and did not create a new tenancy or extinguish an existing tenant’s purchase rights.
The tenants were entitled to exercise their statutory purchase right after the Watan lands were regranted, and the regrant order did not need to be challenged by them.
